title: Corrective Action Plan (CAP) Preparation
subtitle: Guidance for preparing a CAP (CAAN SMS Implementation Guidance Material, March 2019)
overview: A CAP documents how an assigned finding or safety concern will be addressed, including root causes, actions, owners, dates and evidence.

CAAN principles (application-specific fields may vary): understand the finding, identify causes, define corrective actions, assign responsibility and dates, identify evidence, and verify effectiveness.

method.title: Method & Preparation Rules
paragraphs: Understand the assigned finding or safety concern before drafting actions.
Identify contributing factors and underlying causes rather than symptoms.
Define corrective actions that directly address those causes.
Assign responsibilities and realistic completion dates.
Identify implementation evidence and how completion/effectiveness will be verified.
bullets: CAAN §3.5.6: investigation responsibilities and corrective actions.
CAAN §3.6: safety risk assessment and mitigation.

mapping.title: Application Mapping
paragraphs: The CAP form fields (action plan, timeline, resources, root causes, action items, residual risk) are application-specific and support the CAAN principles above.

example.title: Worked Example
paragraphs: Finding: FOD repeatedly observed on apron near Gate 3.
CAP: daily FOD sweep procedure, checklist, sweep logs as evidence, short-term mitigation and long-term fix; root cause promoted to control measure; sign-off and closure.
